open_findings.description: Late lease application reproduced with unchanged identity; independent scheduler and observed-cost margin validated by source and installed tests. Full load qualification remains in M7/M8.
Startup test now observes retained recovery worker result with bounded wait; installed restart cases passed.

Two Pi warm replacements failed BINDING_NOT_AUTHORIZED during M1 live UI campaign, without birth records; later refill succeeded automatically. Exact refusal frontier absent from receipts; not attributed to L1 without evidence.

M2e live HTTP startup waited about 2m20s for initial Pi build-identity inventory scan; stack dump confirms dependency through EmbeddedInventoryOwner.start. Separate owner claim from background initial discovery with retry and retained shutdown. M3c global rollout and second normal boot served HTTP before per-agent recovery; see m3c-ui-recovery.md.

M2e real Codex request delivered and acknowledged, but provider returned usageLimitExceeded. Pi and Claude succeeded. Full three-provider UI success cannot be claimed; no quota bypass or repeated requests.

Local contact is now refreshed only by current owner heartbeat; stale or replaced owner cannot preserve Ready. 46 source/installed cases passed (M3d), global rollout pending. Accessible ACK discrepancy did not recur in M3c; no ACK fix claimed.

M2e Pi recurrence diagnosed: three claimed openings without births had no original-owner containment path after native factory failure. Shared Core fix passed installed process tests. Joint M3c rollout automatically contained all three retained launches; Pi and Claude replied via Meta-harness. M3c then shut down gracefully in 6.46s and recovered all agents after restart, with a fresh Pi response. Initial CONFIG_ERROR subtype remains unproven. See m3c-ui-recovery.md.

M3c generation 68 process absent when UI was revisited, last access log 20:58:19 UTC, no recorded normal shutdown/traceback or matching Application Error event. Cause/initiator unproven. Logs preserved; generation 69 recovered all agents and Pi answered. Supervisor/host-lifetime qualification must distinguish host termination from runtime faults.

Generation 69: RECOVERY_PUBLICATION_DELAYED diagnostic write timed out and escalated to host containment, stranding all local agents. M3f makes transient diagnostic persistence best-effort without changing receipt/authority durability. Origin of initial writer delay unproven. Global generation 70 recovered all agents; Graph presence confirmed. Pi and Claude replied through the real Meta-harness with 1/1 ACK on generation 70. M4d2 narrows diagnostic fallback to RECOVERY_PUBLICATION_DELAYED only; other durable recovery evidence stays required.

An already-contained embedded owner has no automatic replacement while HTTP remains alive. Initial-start recovery is not post-containment supervision. Need retained producer join/resource release proof before replacement; M3f prevents the observed diagnostic trigger and stops manual recovery falsely reporting READY, but does not implement general owner replacement. Generation 69 also remained DRAINING_PENDING after normal shutdown despite zero occupied slots/active turns and no server child processes; exact PID termination was needed for deployment. Preserved stacks; no lock reset.

First global M4d1 migration: Pi stayed RECOVERING until 03:03:20.844Z after host ready at 02:54:18Z. Closed-history retirement still precedes agent READY; certificates progressed 3/18/55 then readiness after first page. Move verified historical maintenance outside admission while retaining exact release/publication proofs; qualify with real retained history. CPU was saturated in one observation, not an attribution of the complete delay. M4d2 separates historical checkpoints from READY and live response publication; 50 installed tests passed. Real retained-history latency qualification remains pending.

Agents initially displayed old RECOVERING until Refresh Agents while all three backend recovery rows were READY; subsequent view mount showed ONLINE. Existing poll pauses when document.hidden; cause not yet attributed and no frontend fix claimed.

Generation 70 Pi has four warm STARTING slots with FAILED/NONE sessions, terminal dispatch refusals (CONFLICT, possible_effect=false) and no Core receipts. Pool settlement recognizes CLOSED lease or failed Core receipt but misses pre-Core refusal. Pi UI response used fifth on-demand slot. Require exact durable no-send proof, never infer safe release from FAILED/NONE alone. Exact message matched dispatch inventory freshness refusal. M3g recognizes the terminal pre-Core refusal with no lease, stream, receipt or publication; 18 installed tests passed. Current global process has not yet loaded this fix.
